Beter Einders Connecting South Africans

By: Hamilton Wende | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on CarteBlanche we look at how South Africans are taking an old theme and trying new ways to connect

Unique Selling Point:
Black and white South Africans meeting over rugby and soccer. A cliche from the days of the Rainbow Nation, but it still has the power to find new ways to understand one another.

Summary:
So we talked about the BeterEinders a few months back https://www.betereinders.co.za/ They have a great number of initiatives: fixing potholes, teaching maths, building schools and so on.
All good for a story but Johan Erasmus, their founder just pitched a story to me that I think would be very visual.

Firstly, let me say that I worked with these BeterEinder guys for a Belgian outfit last winter and they strike me as people who have immense integrity and really believe in making South Africa work – or at least, finding ways to contribute to that goal. This is something we all need in this country at this moment in our history, and there are far too few voices trying to hold hope together which these guys are doing – as I said they have a number of ongoing projects which make a nice story but the initiative they have told me about below really has the potential to be visually and emotionally exciting.

Their mission is to bring South Africans together, so with this in mind they have a two fold initiative. Firstly on 18 Feb they have bought 120 tickets for the Bulls and Stormers match at Loftus. And then on 18 March they will take a group of people to the Sundowns Royal AM match. The idea is to get a predominantly white crowd to introduce their black friends to rugby and a predominantly black crowd to introduce their friends to soccer.

It is organized through their somewhat informal church which meets at the Pretoria rugby club every Sunday but on Saturday 18 Feb they will have a braai starting at 15:00 at the club and everyone will get together. They will have a couple of loose touch rugby games to introduce people who don’t know rugby to the rules etc of the game. And then the group of them will walk to Loftus (its not far a couple of kms) and the idea is that everyone should speak to someone they don’t know says Johan and then they will watch the game together and discuss afterwards.

People are coming from Thembisa and other townships in the Pretoria area and Johan is confident he will get a decent showing.

And then on 18 March the process is repeated except over soccer.

I think we could profile a person or group coming from the township who’s very unfamiliar with rugby and follow him/her/them to the braai and through the whole excitement of the match etc and, of course segue into Johan and others along the way.

We do that for both events and end with some sort of wrap of feelings, thoughts about what its like to encounter other South Africans and what it means for where we are as a country today.

Much real, hard work needs to be done to address the unsolved inequalities and the racial divisions of our past.

Johan Erasmus from Pretoria is someone willing to engage in the difficult work and at least open up the truly important conversations that need to be had.

His group, Beter Einders, works to find ways to reconcile the past and create a better future for us all.

Their name is a play on the Bitter Einders who refused to surrender in the dying days of the Anglo-Boer War

metadata.Summary: So we talked about the BeterEinders a few months back https://www.betereinders.co.za/ They have a great number of initiatives: fixing potholes, teaching maths, building schools and so on. All good for a story but Johan Erasmus, their founder just pitched a story to me that I think would be very visual. Firstly, let me say that I worked with these BeterEinder guys for a Belgian outfit last winter and they strike me as people who have immense integrity and really believe in making South Africa work – or at least, finding ways to contribute to that goal. This is something we all need in this country at this moment in our history, and there are far too few voices trying to hold hope together which these guys are doing – as I said they have a number of ongoing projects which make a nice story but the initiative they have told me about below really has the potential to be visually and emotionally exciting. Their mission is to bring South Africans together, so with this in mind they have a two fold initiative. Firstly on 18 Feb they have bought 120 tickets for the Bulls and Stormers match at Loftus. And then on 18 March they will take a group of people to the Sundowns Royal AM match. The idea is to get a predominantly white crowd to introduce their black friends to rugby and a predominantly black crowd to introduce their friends to soccer. It is organized through their somewhat informal church which meets at the Pretoria rugby club every Sunday but on Saturday 18 Feb they will have a braai starting at 15:00 at the club and everyone will get together. They will have a couple of loose touch rugby games to introduce people who don’t know rugby to the rules etc of the game. And then the group of them will walk to Loftus (its not far a couple of kms) and the idea is that everyone should speak to someone they don’t know says Johan and then they will watch the game together and discuss afterwards. People are coming from Thembisa and other townships in the Pretoria area and Johan is confident he will get a decent showing. And then on 18 March the process is repeated except over soccer. I think we could profile a person or group coming from the township who’s very unfamiliar with rugby and follow him/her/them to the braai and through the whole excitement of the match etc and, of course segue into Johan and others along the way. We do that for both events and end with some sort of wrap of feelings, thoughts about what its like to encounter other South Africans and what it means for where we are as a country today.
